gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-mukta-ma: Love Ya Like A Sister draws a thread of ink with no swelling or tapering, bold in attitude but level in stroke. And Mukta Mahee follows with chunky, tall lowercase letters that give the pair its real weight.

gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-mukta-va: Ribbon-cut and brash, Love Ya Like A Sister holds every stroke to a constant width. But Mukta Vaani, a plain sans with a high-waisted lowercase, gives the pair its sharpest quality: contemporary restraint beneath loud display letters.

gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-ramabhad: Ramabhadra has a prominent x-height, clean and professional in its sans build. Ramabhadra would read steadily over a long passage, with no pressure swells in the heading above to make the eye slow down.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-rambla: Love Ya Like A Sister is drawn with one fixed nib, bold yet restrained. Rambla, a sans-serif whose small letters stand almost as tall as capitals, adds a clean, neutral counterweight that is the pair's best quality.
